This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
editorial_review.policy: The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

verses.text:
1:2 For He is found by those who do not put Him to the test,
and He makes Himself known to those who do not distrust Him.

1:3 For crooked reasonings separate from God,
and power, when put to the test, exposes the foolish.

1:4 For wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil,
nor will she dwell in a body indebted to sin.

1:5 For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit
and depart from senseless reasonings,
and will be put to shame when injustice comes upon it.

1:7 For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world,
and that which holds all things together has knowledge of utterance.

1:8 Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will escape notice,
nor will convicting justice pass him by.

1:9 For there will be an examination of the ungodly person’s deliberations,
and the report of his words will come to the Lord
to expose his lawless deeds.

1:10 For an ear of jealousy listens to all things,
and the murmur of grumblings is not hidden.

1:12 Do not pursue death through the wandering of your life,
nor draw destruction upon yourselves through the works of your hands;

1:13 For God did not make death,
neither does He delight in the destruction of the living.

1:14 For He created all things that they might exist,
and the created things of the world are life-preserving;
there is no poison of destruction in them,
nor is Hades’ dominion upon the earth.
1:15 For righteousness is immortal.

1:16 But the ungodly summoned him by their hands and words;
considering him a friend, they wasted away,
and they made a covenant with him,
because they are worthy to belong to his portion.

verses.text:
2:1 For they said among themselves, reasoning wrongly:
“Our life is short and sorrowful,
and there is no healing when a human being dies,
and no one has been known to return from Hades.

2:3 when it is extinguished, the body will become ashes,
and the spirit will disperse like insubstantial air.

2:4 And our name will be forgotten in time,
and no one will remember our works;
our life will pass like the traces of a cloud,
and will disperse like mist,
driven away by the sun’s rays
and weighed down by its heat.

2:5 For our allotted time is the passing of a shadow,
and there is no turning back from our end,
because it has been sealed, and no one returns.

2:6 Come, then, and let us enjoy the good things that exist,
and eagerly make use of creation as in youth.

2:7 Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes,
and let no spring blossom pass us by.
2:8 Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.

2:11 Let our strength be the law of righteousness,
for what is weak is shown to be useless.

2:12 Let us lie in wait for the righteous person, because he is troublesome to us
and opposes our works;
he reproaches us for sins against law
and charges us with sins against our upbringing.

2:13 He professes to have knowledge of God
and calls himself a child of the Lord.

2:14 He has become a reproach to our thoughts;
even the sight of him weighs upon us,

2:15 because his life is unlike that of others,
and his paths are different.

2:16 He has reckoned us counterfeit,
and keeps away from our ways as from impurities;
he calls the final lot of the righteous blessed,
and boasts that God is his father.

2:17 Let us see whether his words are true,
and test what will happen at his departure.

2:18 For if the righteous person is a son of God, He will help him
and rescue him from the hand of his opponents.

2:19 Let us examine him with insult and torture,
so that we may know his gentleness
and test his endurance of wrong.

2:20 Let us condemn him to a shameful death,
for, according to his words, he will be visited with care.”

2:21 They reasoned these things and went astray,
for their wickedness blinded them;

2:22 they did not know the mysteries of God,
nor hope for a reward of holiness,
nor recognize a prize for blameless souls.

2:23 For God created the human being for incorruption
and made him an image of His own eternity;

2:24 but through the devil’s envy death entered the world,
and those who belong to his portion experience it.

verses.text: 3:1 But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment will surely not touch them.

3:2 In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died,
and their departure was reckoned a calamity,

3:3 and their going away from us a destruction;
but they are in peace.

3:4 For even if they are punished in the sight of human beings,
their hope is full of immortality;

3:5 and after being disciplined a little, they will receive great benefits,
because God tested them
and found them worthy of Himself.

3:6 Like gold in a crucible He tested them,
and like a sacrificial whole burnt offering He accepted them.

3:7 And at the time of their visitation they will shine out,
and like sparks among stubble they will dart about.

3:8 They will judge nations and rule over peoples,
and the Lord will reign over them unto the ages.

3:9 Those who trust in Him will understand truth,
and the faithful will remain with Him in love,
for grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.

3:10 But the ungodly will have punishment in keeping with their reasoning—
those who neglected what is righteous and departed from the Lord.

3:15 For the fruit of good labors is glorious,
and the root of understanding does not fail.

3:16 But the children of adulterers will not reach fulfillment,
and offspring from an unlawful bed will disappear.

3:17 For even if they become long-lived, they will be reckoned as nothing,
and their old age will be without honor at the end;

3:18 and if they die quickly, they will have no hope,
nor consolation on the day of decision.
3:19 For the ends of an unrighteous generation are harsh.

verses.text:
4:2 When it is present, people imitate it,
and when it has departed, they long for it;
throughout the age it marches crowned in triumph,
having won the contest for undefiled prizes.

4:4 For even if it flourishes in branches for a time,
standing insecurely, it will be shaken by wind
and uprooted by the force of winds.

4:5 Unfulfilled branches will be broken off,
and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating,
and fit for nothing.

4:6 For children born from unlawful unions
are witnesses of wickedness against their parents at their examination.
4:7 But if a righteous person dies early, he will be at rest.

4:8 For honorable old age is not length of time,
nor is it measured by a number of years;

4:9 rather, understanding is gray hair for human beings,
and an unstained life is the maturity of old age.

4:10 Having become pleasing to God, he was loved,
and while living among sinners he was transferred.

4:11 He was snatched away, lest evil change his understanding
or deceit mislead his soul;

4:12 for the fascination of wickedness obscures what is good,
and the wandering of desire alters an innocent mind.
4:13 Having been brought to completion in a short time, he fulfilled long years;

4:14 for his soul was pleasing to the Lord;
therefore he hastened from the midst of wickedness.
Yet the peoples saw and did not understand,
nor set such a thing in their minds:

4:15 that grace and mercy are among His chosen ones,
and visitation among His holy ones.

4:16 But a righteous person who has died will condemn the living ungodly,
and youth brought swiftly to completion will condemn the many years of an unrighteous person’s old age.

4:17 For they will see a wise person’s end
and will not understand what the Lord planned concerning him
or for what purpose He kept him safe.

4:18 They will see and despise,
but the Lord will laugh them to scorn.

4:20 They will come in dread at the reckoning of their sins,
and their lawless deeds will confront and convict them.

verses.text:
5:1 Then the righteous person will stand with great boldness
before those who afflicted him
and those who disregarded his labors.

5:2 When they see him, they will be troubled with terrible fear
and astonished at his unexpected salvation.

5:3 They will speak among themselves in repentance,
and in anguish of spirit they will groan and say:

5:4 “This was the one whom we fools once made a laughingstock
and a byword of reproach.
We reckoned his life madness
and his end dishonorable.

5:5 How was he counted among the sons of God,
and how is his portion among the saints?

5:6 So we strayed from the way of truth,
and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us,
and the sun did not rise upon us.

5:7 We were filled with paths of lawlessness and destruction,
and traveled through trackless deserts,
but the way of the Lord we did not know.

5:8 What did arrogance profit us?
And what did wealth with boasting contribute to us?

5:9 All those things passed like a shadow
and like a report rushing by;

5:12 or like an arrow shot at a target:
the air it cut immediately flowed back into itself,
so that its course could not be known:

5:13 so we also were born and vanished,
and had no sign of virtue to show,
but were consumed in our wickedness.”

5:14 For the hope of an ungodly person is like dust borne by wind,
and like fine frost driven by a storm;
like smoke it was dispersed by wind,
and like the memory of a guest who stayed one day it passed away.

5:15 But the righteous live for ever,
and their reward is with the Lord,
and the Most High takes care of them.

5:16 Therefore they will receive the royal crown of splendor
and the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand,
because with His right hand He will cover them
and with His arm He will shield them.

5:17 He will take His zeal as full armor
and make creation into weapons to repel His enemies;

5:18 He will put on righteousness as a breastplate,
and put on unfeigned judgment as a helmet;
5:19 He will take holiness as an invincible shield,

5:20 and sharpen stern wrath into a sword;
the world will fight together with Him against the senseless.

5:21 Well-aimed bolts of lightning will go forth,
and from the clouds, as from a well-curved bow, they will leap at the target;

5:23 A mighty wind will oppose them
and winnow them away like a storm;
lawlessness will lay the whole earth waste,
and wrongdoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.

verses.text:
6:1 Listen, then, kings, and understand;
learn, judges of the ends of the earth.

6:2 Give ear, you who rule a multitude
and boast over crowds of nations;

6:3 for your rule was given you by the Lord,
and your authority by the Most High,
who will examine your works and search out your plans.

6:4 For though you were servants of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly,
nor keep law,
nor walk according to God’s purpose.

6:5 He will come upon you terribly and swiftly,
for a severe judgment falls upon those in high position.

6:6 For the least is pardonable through mercy,
but the powerful will be powerfully examined.

6:7 For the Master of all will not shrink before anyone’s face
or show deference to greatness,
because He Himself made both small and great
and provides for all alike;
6:8 but a forceful inquiry awaits the mighty.

6:9 To you, therefore, rulers, my words are directed,
so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.

6:10 For those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy,
and those instructed in them will find a defense.

6:11 Desire my words, then;
long for them, and you will be instructed.
6:13 She goes ahead of those who desire her, making herself known first.

6:14 The one who rises early for her will not grow weary,
for he will find her sitting beside his gates.

6:15 For to reflect upon her is the perfection of understanding,
and the one who keeps watch for her will soon be free from care;

6:16 for she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her,
appears graciously to them on their paths,
and meets them in every thought.

6:17 For her beginning is the truest desire for discipline,
and concern for discipline is love;

6:18 love is the keeping of her laws,
and attention to laws is assurance of incorruption;
6:19 and incorruption brings one near to God.
6:20 Therefore desire for wisdom leads up to kingship.

6:21 If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, rulers of peoples,
honor wisdom, so that you may reign for ever.

6:22 What wisdom is and how she came to be, I will declare,
and I will not hide mysteries from you;
instead I will trace her from the beginning of her origin,
and bring the knowledge of her into the open,
and I will certainly not pass truth by.

6:23 Nor will I travel with wasting envy,
for it will have no share with wisdom.

6:24 A multitude of wise people is the world’s salvation,
and an understanding king is the stability of a people.
6:25 Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will benefit.

verses.text:
7:2 taking form in blood over a time of ten months,
from a man’s seed and the pleasure that accompanied sleep.

7:3 And when I was born, I drew in the common air
and fell upon the earth that shares the same lot,
crying as my first sound just like everyone else.
7:4 I was brought up in swaddling clothes and attentive care.
7:5 For no king had a different beginning of birth;
7:6 all have one entrance into life, and the same departure.

7:7 Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me;
I called out, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.

7:8 I preferred her to scepters and thrones,
and reckoned wealth as nothing in comparison with her.

7:10 I loved her more than health and beauty,
and chose to have her rather than light,
because the radiance that comes from her never sleeps.

7:11 But all good things came to me together with her,
and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.

7:12 I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom leads them,
but I did not know that she was their mother.

7:13 I learned without deceit and share without envy;
I do not conceal her wealth.

7:15 May God grant me to speak with judgment
and to reflect worthily on what has been given,
for He is both the guide of wisdom
and the corrector of the wise.

7:16 For in His hand are both we and our words,
all understanding and skill in crafts.

7:17 For He Himself gave me unerring knowledge of existing things:
to know the composition of the world and the activity of the elements,

7:18 the beginning and end and middle of times,
the changes of the solstices and the transitions of seasons,
7:19 the cycles of the year and the positions of stars,

7:20 the natures of living creatures and the tempers of wild animals,
the forces of winds and the reasonings of human beings,
the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.

7:21 I learned all that is hidden and manifest,
for wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me.

7:22 For in her is a spirit intelligent, holy,
unique, manifold, subtle,
agile, lucid, undefiled,
clear, unharmed, loving the good, keen,

7:23 unhindered, beneficent, loving humanity,
steadfast, secure, free from care,
all-powerful, all-overseeing,
and passing through all spirits
that are intelligent, pure, and most subtle.

7:24 For wisdom is more mobile than every motion;
she penetrates and passes through all things because of her purity.

7:26 For she is a radiance of eternal light,
an unstained mirror of God’s activity,
and an image of His goodness.

7:27 Though she is one, she can do all things;
remaining in herself, she renews all things,
and passing into holy souls from generation to generation,
she makes friends of God and prophets.
7:28 For God loves no one except the one who dwells with wisdom.

7:30 For night succeeds light,
but evil does not overpower wisdom.

verses.text: 8:1 She reaches mightily from end to end, and governs all things well.

8:2 I loved her and sought her out from my youth,
and sought to take her as my bride,
and became a lover of her beauty.

8:3 She glorifies her noble birth by sharing life with God,
and the Master of all loved her;

8:4 for she is initiated into God’s knowledge
and is a chooser of His works.

8:5 If wealth is a desirable possession in life,
what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?

8:6 And if understanding accomplishes things,
who among existing beings is more skilled than she?

8:9 Therefore I decided to take her to live with me,
knowing that she would be a counselor of good things to me
and encouragement amid cares and sorrow.

8:10 Through her I will have glory among the crowds,
and, though young, honor among elders.

8:11 I will be found keen in judgment
and will be admired in the sight of rulers.

8:13 Through her I will have immortality,
and will leave an everlasting remembrance to those after me.
8:14 I will govern peoples, and nations will be subjected to me.

8:15 Terrifying rulers will fear me when they hear of me;
among the multitude I will appear good, and in war courageous.

8:17 Having reasoned these things within myself
and considered in my heart
that immortality is in kinship with wisdom,

8:18 and in friendship with her is good delight,
and in the labors of her hands unfailing wealth,
and in the shared exercise of companionship with her understanding,
and in sharing her words good renown,
I went about seeking how to take her to myself.

8:19 I was a naturally gifted child,
and received a good soul as my lot;
8:20 or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.

8:21 But knowing that I could not otherwise gain possession of her unless God gave her—
and this too was understanding: to know whose gift it was—
I appealed to the Lord and petitioned Him,
and said with my whole heart:

verses.text:
9:1 “God of the fathers and Lord of mercy,
who made all things by Thy word

9:2 and by Thy wisdom fashioned the human being,
so that he might rule over the creatures made by Thee

9:3 and administer the world in holiness and righteousness,
and render judgment in uprightness of soul,

9:4 give me wisdom, who sits beside Thy thrones,
and do not reject me from among Thy servants.

9:5 For I am Thy slave and the son of Thy slave woman,
a weak and short-lived human being,
deficient in understanding judgment and laws.

9:6 For even if someone is perfect among the sons of human beings,
without the wisdom that comes from Thee, he will be reckoned as nothing.

9:7 Thou didst choose me as king of Thy people
and judge of Thy sons and daughters.

9:8 Thou didst tell me to build a temple on Thy holy mountain
and an altar in the city of Thy dwelling,
a likeness of the holy tent that Thou didst prepare beforehand from the beginning.

9:9 With Thee is wisdom, who knows Thy works
and was present when Thou didst make the world,
who understands what is pleasing in Thine eyes
and what is upright in Thy commandments.

9:10 Send her out from the holy heavens,
and from the throne of Thy glory send her,
so that she may labor at my side,
and I may know what is pleasing to Thee.

9:12 and my works will be acceptable,
and I will judge Thy people righteously
and be worthy of my father’s thrones.

9:13 For what human being will know God’s purpose?
Or who will conceive what the Lord wills?

9:14 For the reasonings of mortals are uncertain,
and our thoughts precarious;

9:15 for a corruptible body weighs down a soul,
and the earthly tent burdens a mind full of cares.

9:17 And who knew Thy purpose, unless Thou didst give wisdom
and send Thy Holy Spirit from on high?

9:18 And in this way the paths of those on earth were set right,
and human beings were taught what pleases Thee,
and were saved by wisdom.”

verses.text: 10:2 and she gave him strength to rule over all things.

10:3 But an unrighteous man, departing from her in his anger,
perished with the passions that made him kill his brother.

10:4 Because of him the earth was being flooded, but wisdom again saved it,
steering the righteous man by means of humble wood.

10:5 When nations were confounded in their shared wickedness,
she recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God,
and preserved him strong against compassion for his child.

10:6 When the ungodly were being destroyed, she rescued a righteous man
who fled the fire descending upon the Five Cities.

10:7 As a witness to its wickedness there still stands a smoking wasteland,
and plants whose fruit never reaches ripeness,
and a standing pillar of salt, a memorial to a disbelieving soul.

10:8 For by passing wisdom by,
they were harmed not only by failing to know what is good,
but also left life a memorial of their folly,
so that even in the things in which they failed they could not escape notice.
10:9 But wisdom rescued those who served her from troubles.

10:11 She stood beside him against those who overpowered him in their greed,
and made him rich.

10:12 She guarded him from enemies
and kept him safe from those lying in wait;
she presided over a mighty contest for him,
so that he might know that devotion to God is stronger than everything.

10:13 She did not abandon a righteous man who had been sold,
but rescued him from sin;

10:14 she went down with him into a pit
and did not leave him in bonds,
until she brought him the scepters of kingship
and authority over those who ruled him;
she showed those who accused him to be liars
and gave him everlasting glory.

10:15 She rescued a holy people and blameless offspring
from a nation of oppressors;

10:16 she entered the soul of a servant of the Lord
and opposed terrifying kings with wonders and signs.

10:17 She repaid the holy ones the reward of their labors,
guided them on a marvelous way,
and became for them a covering by day
and a flame of stars by night.

10:18 She brought them across the Red Sea
and led them through abundant water;

10:19 but their enemies she overwhelmed with the flood
and cast them up from the depth of the abyss.

10:21 for wisdom opened the mouth of the mute
and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.

verses.text: 11:1 She prospered their works by the hand of a holy prophet.

11:2 They traveled through an uninhabited desert
and pitched tents in trackless places;
11:3 they opposed their adversaries and repelled their enemies.

11:4 They thirsted and called upon Thee,
and water was given them from a sheer rock,
and a cure for thirst from hard stone.

11:5 For through the very things by which their enemies were punished,
they themselves received benefits in their need.

11:6 Instead of the source of an ever-flowing river
turbid with bloody gore,

11:7 as a rebuke to the decree for killing infants,
Thou didst give them abundant water beyond their expectation,

11:8 showing through the thirst of that time
how Thou didst punish their opponents.

11:9 For when they were tested, although disciplined in mercy,
they learned how the ungodly were tormented when judged in wrath.

11:10 For these Thou didst test as a father giving instruction,
but those Thou didst examine as a stern king condemning them.
11:11 Whether absent or present, they were worn down alike;

11:12 for a twofold sorrow seized them,
and a groaning at the remembrance of what had passed.

11:13 For when they heard that the others had received benefits through their own punishments,
they became aware of the Lord.

11:14 For the one long ago cast out in exposure, whom they rejected with mockery,
they marveled at in the final outcome,
having thirsted unlike the righteous.

11:15 In return for the senseless reasonings of their unrighteousness,
in which they went astray and worshiped irrational creeping things and worthless beasts,
Thou didst send upon them a multitude of irrational animals for vengeance,
11:16 so that they might know that through the things by which someone sins, through those things he is punished.

11:17 For Thine all-powerful hand,
which created the world from unformed matter,
was not at a loss to send upon them a multitude of bears or fierce lions,

11:18 or newly created, unknown beasts full of fury,
either breathing a fire-breathing blast,
or scattering a stench of smoke,
or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes,

11:19 whose injury could not only utterly crush them,
but whose very appearance could terrify and destroy them.

11:20 Even without these, they could have fallen at a single breath,
pursued by justice
and winnowed away by the breath of Thy power;
but Thou didst arrange all things by measure and number and weight.

11:21 For great strength is always at Thy disposal,
and who will oppose the might of Thine arm?

11:22 For the whole world before Thee is like a slight tipping of the scales,
and like a drop of morning dew that has fallen upon the earth.

11:23 But Thou hast mercy on all, because Thou canst do all things,
and Thou overlookest human sins with a view to repentance.

11:25 How could anything have endured unless Thou didst will it,
or what had not been called by Thee have been preserved?
11:26 But Thou sparest all things, because they are Thine, Master who loves life.

verses.text: 12:1 For Thine incorruptible Spirit is in all things.

12:2 Therefore Thou reprovest those who fall away little by little,
and admonishest them by reminding them of the things in which they sin,
so that, freed from evil, they may believe in Thee, Lord.
12:3 For the ancient inhabitants of Thy holy land,

12:4 whom Thou didst hate for practicing the most detestable things—
works of sorcery and unholy rites,

12:5 merciless murders of children,
and an entrail-devouring feast of human flesh and blood—
initiates from the midst of a ritual company,

12:6 and parents who were murderers of helpless lives,
Thou didst will to destroy by the hands of our fathers,

12:7 so that the land most precious to Thee of all
might receive a worthy settlement of God’s children.

12:8 Yet even these Thou didst spare as human beings,
and send hornets as forerunners of Thine army,
so that they might destroy them little by little.

12:9 Thou wast not unable to give the ungodly into the hands of the righteous in battle,
or to crush them all at once with terrifying beasts or a stern word;

12:10 but judging them little by little, Thou didst give room for repentance,
not unaware that their origin was wicked,
and their evil ingrained,
and that their reasoning would never change.

12:11 For they were an accursed offspring from the beginning;
nor was it out of fear of anyone that Thou didst grant them respite for their sins.

12:12 For who will say, ‘What hast Thou done?’
Or who will oppose Thy judgment?
Who will accuse Thee concerning destroyed nations that Thou didst make?
Or who will come to confront Thee as an avenger concerning unrighteous human beings?

12:13 For there is no god besides Thee, who cares for all,
so that Thou shouldst have to show that Thou hast not judged unjustly;
12:14 nor will a king or ruler be able to face Thee concerning those Thou didst punish.

12:15 But being righteous, Thou administerest all things righteously,
regarding it as alien to Thy power
to condemn anyone who does not deserve punishment.

12:16 For Thy strength is the beginning of righteousness,
and Thy mastery over all makes Thee spare all.

12:17 For Thou displayest strength when the completeness of Thy power is disbelieved,
and among those who know, Thou exposest their audacity.

12:19 Through such works Thou didst teach Thy people
that the righteous person must love humanity,
and make Thy sons hopeful,
because Thou givest repentance for sins.

12:20 For if Thou didst punish the enemies of Thy children, who were liable to death,
with such attention and leniency,
giving times and room through which they might be freed from evil,

12:21 with how much care didst Thou judge Thy sons,
to whose fathers Thou didst give oaths and covenants of good promises?

12:22 Therefore, while disciplining us, Thou scourgest our enemies with myriad blows,
so that when judging we may consider Thy goodness,
and when judged we may expect mercy.

12:23 Therefore those who lived unrighteously in a foolish way of life
Thou didst also torment through their own abominations.

12:24 For they wandered even farther than the paths of error,
supposing that creatures despised even among shameful animals were gods,
deceived like senseless infants.

12:25 Therefore, as to children without reason,
Thou didst send judgment in mockery.

12:26 But those who were not admonished by playful reproofs
will experience a judgment worthy of God.

12:27 For as they suffered punishment through the very creatures
they had supposed to be gods, they grew indignant at them,
and saw and recognized as the true God the One they had long refused to know;
therefore the final condemnation also came upon them.

verses.text:
13:2 Instead, they supposed fire or wind or swift-moving air,
or the circuit of stars or violent water,
or the lights of heaven to be gods, rulers of the world.

13:4 And if they were astonished at their power and activity,
let them understand from these how much more powerful the One who fashioned them is.

13:5 For from the greatness and beauty of created things
their Maker is seen by analogy.

13:6 Yet the blame upon these is small,
for perhaps they themselves go astray
while seeking God and wishing to find Him.

13:7 For living among His works, they search them out
and are persuaded by their appearance, because the things seen are beautiful.
13:8 But again, even they are not excusable;

13:9 for if they were able to know so much
that they could investigate the world,
how did they not more quickly find the Master of these things?

13:10 But wretched are those whose hopes rest in dead things,
who called the works of human hands gods:
gold and silver, exercises of craftsmanship,
likenesses of living creatures,
or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.

13:11 Suppose a woodcutting craftsman sawed down a manageable tree,
skillfully scraped off all its bark,
and, working it handsomely,
fashioned a useful vessel for the service of life,

13:12 and burned the scraps from the work
to prepare food and ate his fill,

13:13 then took the scrap left from these, useful for nothing,
a crooked piece of wood grown full of knots,
and carved it with the care of his leisure,
shaped it with practiced understanding,
and made it resemble a human image,

13:14 or made it like some worthless animal,
coating it with red ocher and reddening its surface with paint,
and covering every blemish in it,

13:15 and made for it a dwelling worthy of it,
set it in a wall, and secured it with iron.

13:19 and for gain, work, and success of his hands,
he asks vigor of what is most powerless with its hands.

verses.text:
14:1 Again, someone preparing for a voyage and about to traverse wild waves
calls upon a piece of wood more rotten than the ship carrying him.

14:2 For the desire for gain devised that ship,
and wisdom, the artisan, fashioned it;

14:3 but Thy providence, Father, steers it,
for Thou didst give a way even in the sea
and a safe path among the waves,

14:4 showing that Thou canst save from every danger,
so that even someone without skill may embark.

14:6 For even at the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing,
the hope of the world took refuge on a raft
and left to the age a seed for generation, steered by Thy hand.
14:7 For blessed is wood through which righteousness comes about;

14:8 but the handmade object is accursed, both it and its maker:
the one because he made it,
and the other because, though corruptible, it was named a god.
14:9 For equally hateful to God are the ungodly person and his ungodliness;
14:10 for what was done will be punished together with the one who did it.

14:11 Therefore there will also be a visitation upon the nations’ idols,
because within God’s creation they became an abomination,
stumbling blocks to human souls,
and a snare for the feet of fools.

14:12 For the devising of idols is the beginning of sexual immorality,
and their invention the corruption of life.

14:13 For they did not exist from the beginning,
nor will they exist for ever;

14:14 through human vainglory they entered the world,
and therefore a swift end was planned for them.

14:15 For a father worn down by untimely grief,
having made an image of a child swiftly taken away,
now honored as a god the one who had once been a dead human being,
and handed on mysteries and rites to those under him.
14:16 Then, strengthened over time, the ungodly custom was kept as law.

14:17 And carved images were worshiped at rulers’ commands;
when people could not honor them face to face because they lived far away,
they reproduced their distant appearance
and made a visible image of the honored king,
so that by their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though present.

14:18 The artist’s ambition urged even those who did not know the king
toward still greater worship;

14:19 for, perhaps wishing to please the ruler,
he used his art to force the likeness toward greater beauty.

14:20 The multitude, drawn by the charm of the workmanship,
now reckoned as an object of worship the human being whom they had honored a little before.

14:21 And this became an ambush for life,
because human beings, enslaved either to misfortune or to royal power,
bestowed upon stones and pieces of wood the name that cannot be shared.

14:23 For while celebrating rites that murder children, or secret mysteries,
or frenzied revelries with strange customs,

14:24 they no longer keep either lives or marriages pure;
one kills another by ambush or grieves him by adultery.

14:25 Bloodshed and murder, theft and deceit, hold everything in confusion,
corruption, unfaithfulness, disturbance, perjury,

14:26 confusion of good things, forgetfulness of favor,
defilement of souls, alteration of natural relations,
disorder in marriages, adultery, and licentiousness.

14:27 For worship of nameless idols
is the beginning, cause, and end of every evil.

14:28 For they either go mad in their merrymaking, or prophesy lies,
or live unjustly, or readily swear falsely.

14:29 For trusting in lifeless idols,
they do not expect to be harmed when they swear wrongly.

14:30 But just consequences will pursue them for both things:
because they thought wrongly about God by attending to idols,
and swore unjustly in deceit, despising holiness.

14:31 For it is not the power of those by whom they swear,
but the justice due to sinners,
that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.

verses.text:
15:1 But Thou, our God, art good and true,
patient, and governing all things in mercy.

15:2 For even if we sin, we are Thine, knowing Thy might;
but we will not sin, knowing that we have been reckoned as Thine.

15:3 For to know Thee is complete righteousness,
and to know Thy might is the root of immortality.

15:4 For neither the evil-devising invention of human beings misled us,
nor the fruitless labor of painters,
a form stained with varied colors,

15:5 the sight of which stirs desire in fools,
and one longs for the breathless form of a dead image.

15:6 Lovers of evil and worthy of such hopes
are those who make them, those who desire them, and those who worship them.

15:8 With evil labor he also shapes a futile god from the same clay,
though he himself, having come from earth a little before,
will shortly go back to that from which he was taken,
when the debt of his soul is demanded.

15:9 But his concern is not that he is about to die,
nor that his life is short;
instead, he competes with goldsmiths and silver-workers,
imitates bronze-workers,
and considers it glory that he fashions counterfeits.

15:10 His heart is ashes, and his hope more worthless than earth,
and his life more dishonorable than clay,

15:11 because he did not know the One who formed him,
who breathed into him an active soul
and breathed in a life-giving spirit.

15:13 For this man knows better than everyone that he is sinning,
when he crafts fragile vessels and carved images from earthy material.

15:14 But all the enemies of Thy people who oppressed them
are most foolish and more wretched than an infant’s soul,

15:15 because they also reckoned all the nations’ idols gods,
though these have neither use of eyes for sight,
nor nostrils for drawing in air,
nor ears to hear,
nor fingers of their hands to feel,
and their feet are idle for walking.

15:18 They also worship the most hateful animals,
for compared in senselessness with the others, these are worse;

15:19 Nor, in their appearance as animals, are they beautiful enough to be desired,
and they have escaped both God’s praise and His blessing.

verses.text:
16:1 Therefore they were deservedly punished through similar creatures
and tormented by a multitude of beasts.

16:2 In contrast to that punishment, Thou didst benefit Thy people:
to meet their eager appetite Thou didst prepare quail as food,
a novel taste,

16:3 so that those, though desiring food,
would turn away even from their necessary appetite
because of the loathsomeness of the creatures sent upon them,
while these, after a brief lack,
would share in a novel taste.

16:4 For unavoidable need had to come upon those who oppressed,
but these only had to be shown how their enemies were tormented.

16:6 they were troubled for a short time as an admonition,
having a symbol of salvation to remind them of the commandment of Thy law.

16:7 For the one who turned toward it was saved not through what was seen,
but through Thee, the Savior of all.

16:8 Through this Thou didst also convince our enemies
that Thou art the One who rescues from every evil.

16:10 but even the teeth of venom-spitting serpents did not conquer Thy sons,
for Thy mercy came to meet them and healed them.

16:11 For they were stung as a reminder of Thine oracles
and swiftly brought safely through,
so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness
and become inattentive to Thy beneficence.

16:12 For neither herb nor poultice healed them,
but Thy word, Lord, which heals all.

16:13 For Thou hast authority over life and death,
and Thou bringest down to the gates of Hades and bringest up again;

16:14 but a human being kills by his wickedness,
and does not bring back a spirit that has gone out,
nor release a soul that has been taken.
16:15 But it is impossible to escape Thy hand.

16:16 For the ungodly, refusing to know Thee,
were scourged by the strength of Thine arm,
pursued by strange rains, hail, and relentless showers,
and consumed by fire.

16:17 Most astonishingly, in water that quenches everything,
the fire worked still more strongly,
for the world fights for the righteous.

16:19 at another time, even amid water, it burns beyond fire’s own power,
so that it may destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.

16:20 In contrast, Thou didst feed Thy people with angels’ food
and supply them ready bread from heaven without toil,
capable of every delight and suited to every taste.

16:22 Snow and ice endured fire and did not melt,
so that they might know that the enemies’ fruits
were destroyed by fire blazing in the hail
and flashing in the rains;

16:23 yet again, so that the righteous might be nourished,
this fire has even forgotten its own power.

16:24 For creation, serving Thee who made it,
strains itself for punishment against the unrighteous
and relaxes itself for benefit on behalf of those who trust in Thee.

16:25 Therefore at that time also, changing into all things,
it served Thy gift that nourishes all,
according to the desire of those in need,

16:26 so that Thy sons whom Thou didst love, Lord, might learn
that it is not the production of fruits that nourishes a human being,
but Thine utterance that preserves those who trust in Thee.

16:27 For what was not destroyed by fire
melted when merely warmed by a brief ray of the sun,

16:28 so that it might be known that one must rise before the sun to give Thee thanks
and appeal to Thee at the rising of the light.

16:29 For the hope of an ungrateful person will melt like wintry frost
and flow away like useless water.

verses.text:
17:1 For Thy judgments are great and hard to recount;
therefore uninstructed souls went astray.

17:2 For lawless people, supposing they could oppress a holy nation,
lay as prisoners of darkness and captives of a long night,
shut under their roofs, fugitives from eternal providence.

17:3 For thinking they could escape notice in secret sins,
under a lightless covering of forgetfulness,
they were scattered, terribly astonished
and shaken by apparitions.

17:5 No force of fire could give light,
nor could the bright flames of stars
endure to illuminate that hateful night.

17:6 Only a self-kindled fire
full of fear shone through to them;
terrified by that unseen sight,
they reckoned what they saw still worse.

17:7 The delusions of magical art lay prostrate,
and its boasting of understanding suffered a scornful exposure;

17:8 for those who promised to drive away the terrors and disturbances of a sick soul
were themselves sick with a ridiculous fear.

17:9 For even if nothing disturbing frightened them,
startled by the passing of beasts and the hissing of creeping things,
they perished trembling,
refusing even to look at the air, which cannot be escaped anywhere.

17:10 For wickedness is a cowardly thing, condemned by its own witness;
pressed by conscience, it always imagines grievous things.
17:11 For fear is nothing but a betrayal of the aids that come from reasoning;

17:12 and as expectation within grows weaker,
it reckons ignorance more fearful than the cause that produces the torment.

17:13 But they, sleeping the same sleep during that truly powerless night,
which had come upon them from the recesses of powerless Hades,

17:15 Then whoever it might be who fell there
was held under guard, shut in a prison without iron bars.

17:16 For whether someone was a farmer or shepherd
or a laborer toiling in the wilderness,
once overtaken, he endured the inescapable compulsion;
for all were bound by one chain of darkness.

17:17 Whether a whistling wind,
or the melodious sound of birds among spreading branches,
or the rhythm of water rushing violently,
or the harsh crash of falling rocks,

17:18 or the unseen running of leaping animals,
or the voice of the fiercest roaring beasts,
or an echo rebounding from the hollows of mountains,
these terrified and paralyzed them.

17:19 For the whole world was illuminated by brilliant light
and occupied with unhindered works;

verses.text:
18:2 and thanked them because, though previously wronged, they did not harm them,
and begged pardon for their quarrel.

18:3 In contrast, Thou didst supply a fire-blazing pillar,
a guide for an unknown journey,
and a harmless sun for a glorious sojourn abroad.

18:4 For those deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness
who had kept Thy sons shut up,
through whom the incorruptible light of law was to be given to the world.

18:5 When they planned to kill the infants of the holy ones,
and one child had been exposed and saved,
Thou didst take away their multitude of children as a rebuke
and destroy them together in violent water.

18:6 That night was known beforehand to our fathers,
so that, knowing securely the oaths in which they trusted, they might take courage.

18:7 Thy people awaited
the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of enemies;

18:8 for by the very means through which Thou didst punish the opponents,
Thou didst glorify us, calling us to Thyself.

18:9 For in secret the holy children of good ancestors offered sacrifice,
and in unity established the divine law:
that the saints would share alike in the same good things and dangers,
already singing beforehand the praises of the fathers.

18:10 But the discordant cry of enemies echoed back,
and a pitiful sound spread abroad as children were mourned.

18:11 Slave and master were punished together by the same judgment,
and the commoner suffered the same things as the king;

18:13 For though they disbelieved everything because of their sorceries,
at the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged that the people were God’s son.

18:14 For while quiet silence surrounded all things
and night was midway through its swift course,

18:16 standing there, it filled all things with death;
it touched heaven while standing upon the earth.

18:17 Then at once apparitions of dreadful dreams disturbed them,
and unexpected fears came upon them;

18:18 one here and another there, hurled down half-dead,
made known the reason why they were dying.

18:19 For the dreams that troubled them had announced this beforehand,
so that they would not perish without knowing why they suffered.

18:21 For a blameless man hastened to fight for them,
bringing the weapon of his own ministry:
prayer and propitiation by incense.
He opposed the wrath and put an end to the calamity,
showing that he was Thy servant.

18:22 He conquered the anger, not by bodily strength,
not by the activity of weapons,
but by a word he subdued the punisher,
reminding him of the fathers’ oaths and covenants.

18:23 For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another,
he stood between them and checked the wrath,
and cut off the path to the living.

18:24 For upon his ankle-length garment was the whole world,
and the glories of the fathers upon the engraving of four rows of stones,
and Thy majesty upon the diadem of his head.

18:25 To these the destroyer yielded, and these he feared;
for the trial of wrath alone was enough.

readingLinks.text: All 30 cross-references for Wisdom of Solomon 19, with the text of each passage →

verses.text:
19:1 But merciless fury came upon the ungodly to the end,
for He knew beforehand even what they would do,

19:2 that after permitting the people to depart
and sending them on their way with haste,
they would change their minds and pursue them.

19:3 For while their griefs were still at hand
and they were lamenting beside the graves of the dead,
they drew upon themselves another senseless plan,
and pursued as fugitives those whom they had begged to leave.

19:4 For the compulsion they deserved drew them toward this end
and cast upon them forgetfulness of what had happened,
so that they might fill up the punishment still lacking in their torments,

19:5 and Thy people might experience an astonishing journey,
while those others found an extraordinary death.

19:6 For the whole creation, in its own kind, was being fashioned anew from the beginning,
serving Thy commands,
so that Thy children might be guarded unharmed.

19:7 The cloud overshadowing the camp was seen,
and dry land rising from water that had existed before,
an unobstructed way out of the Red Sea,
and a grass-bearing plain out of the violent surge;

19:8 through it those sheltered by Thy hand passed as an entire nation,
having seen marvelous wonders.

19:9 For they grazed like horses
and leaped like lambs, praising Thee, Lord, who rescued them.

19:10 For they still remembered the things from their sojourn:
how, instead of producing animals, the earth brought forth gnats,
and instead of aquatic creatures the river disgorged a multitude of frogs.

19:11 Later they also saw a new production of birds,
when, urged on by desire, they asked for luxurious foods;
19:12 for as a consolation quail came up to them from the sea.

19:14 For the former did not receive unfamiliar visitors when they came,
but these enslaved strangers who had benefited them.

19:15 And not only that: there will be a visitation upon the former,
since they received foreigners with hostility;

19:16 but the latter, after receiving with celebrations
those who had already shared in the same rights,
afflicted them with terrible labors.

19:17 They were also struck with blindness,
like those at the righteous man’s doors,
when, surrounded by yawning darkness,
each sought the passage through his own doors.

19:18 For the elements were being rearranged among themselves,
as notes on a harp change the pattern of the rhythm,
while always retaining their sound;
this can be inferred precisely from observing what happened.

19:19 For land creatures were changed into water creatures,
and swimming creatures moved onto land;

19:20 fire in water exceeded its own power,
and water forgot its nature of extinguishing;

19:21 flames, conversely, did not wither the flesh
of perishable animals walking among them,
nor the meltable, crystal-like kind of heavenly food that readily melts.

19:22 For in every way, Lord, Thou didst magnify and glorify Thy people,
and didst not disregard them, standing beside them at every time and place.

index.text:
Wisdom of Solomon

The Holy Bible · III. Wisdom

Bespoke Saints English Translation · 19 chapters · Provisional editorial edition · 15 October 2026

Wisdom of Solomon calls us to love righteousness, seek the wisdom of God, and trust His care through suffering and death. Within the Wisdom division, it joins prayerful discernment to hope in God’s justice and mercy. Christians hear its portrait of the suffering righteous one anew in the passion of Christ and His vindication in the resurrection.

The reading journey

After the lament for Jerusalem, Wisdom of Solomon turns toward the hope of the righteous and God’s care through suffering. Its prayer for wisdom leads naturally into Sirach’s instruction for everyday faithfulness. In this edition, these books bring the Wisdom division toward its close.

Begin Wisdom of Solomon 1 → · Compare Latin and Greek

← Lamentations · III. Wisdom · Sirach →

Draft for review. Only editors can see this introduction. Approve all introductions under Settings → Saints Study.

INTRODUCTION

Introducing Wisdom of Solomon

The Wisdom of Solomon exhorts rulers to love justice and seek Wisdom, God’s radiant gift. It offers a strong hope of immortality for the righteous and reflects on God’s guidance in Israel’s history.

SETTING
Addressed to Jews living in a Hellenistic city, likely Alexandria, it encouraged fidelity to God amid pagan philosophy and idolatry.
AUTHOR
Written in the voice of Solomon. Most scholars, ancient and modern, recognise it as the work of a Greek-speaking Jewish author, probably in Alexandria.
DATE
Probably the 1st century BC, possibly early 1st century AD.

Saints Translation: sources and study approach
Bespoke Saints English editorial guide

All 19 numbered chapters and 435 existing reading units have received the Bespoke English editorial pass: 119 revised and 316 retained. Source-specific numbering, additions, gaps, names, repetitions and verse anchors are preserved. The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending. All English reading units were individually reviewed. Earlier source-checking statements and retrieval limitations are retained in the original backup and historical reference pages; they are not claims of fresh complete verification in this revision.

The newer Bespoke PDF governs this reading edition. Saints Translation literal-smooth and all comparison/study streams remain separate and unchanged. Notes are separated from Scripture. Earlier wording notes are historical records and may quote superseded pronouns or wording; the dated current Bespoke notes explain the changes. The source numbering remains intact, including chapter 17 ending at 17:20. The later KJV Apocrypha comparison is preserved as a separate record; older chooser and study statements that no KJV comparison exists describe an earlier source scope. Historical comparison pages may contain older English drafts and unresolved alignment issues; they are preserved as separate records.

Included in the Old Testament, Division III: Wisdom, in this selected edition. Catholic Scripture; received in many Orthodox Old Testaments; generally classed as Apocrypha outside the Protestant Old Testament canon. This placement is the editor’s selection, not a claim of agreement among all churches.

Source-access and reception claims in the inherited notes have not been freshly revalidated. Chapter and section headings are editorial.
